reason: Melting the sampled ice seems like a useful first step toward separating its solid grains, and it is the only available action.
expectation: I expect the ice sample to melt, leaving the suspended grains available for separation, though I don't know exactly how the game will handle the sample.

effect: Melting released the particles but destroyed their original positions, so I can examine the grains without recovering their arrangement in the ice.
reaction: The loss of positional information is a useful and slightly surprising detail.
reason: Filtering the suspension seems like the natural way to separate its solid grains, and it is the only available combination.
expectation: I expect the cloth to retain the sediment grains while the meltwater passes through, though I don't know how fine the collected material will be.

effect: The filter separated the solids from the meltwater, leaving them crowded together for closer examination.
reaction: The crowded particles make me curious about what the microscope will reveal.
reason: The microscope is the natural way to examine the trapped grains, and this is the only available combination.
expectation: I expect to see details of the collected particles, though their crowded arrangement may make them difficult to distinguish.

effect: The microscope revealed a segmented body with limbs in the band sediment. Because the specimen was damaged on the filter, the plan is now to bring back unmelting ice in hopes of preserving a whole one.
reaction: The discovery was startling, especially after the sample had seemed to be ordinary sediment.

mostWorthwhile.text: Melting the chip was worthwhile because it made the grains accessible while clearly showing that their original positions were lost.

leastWorthwhile.text: Filtering was a straightforward, only-available step; it was useful but less engaging as a decision.

surprise.text: The microscope revealed a body with joints and limbs among what I expected to be sediment grains.

arbitrary.text: None of the actions felt arbitrary, although each step offered only one gameplay combination.

continue.text: Yes. I would want to know what the body is and whether intact ice preserves a whole specimen; the discovery also makes the sample-handling tradeoff matter.
